findings.reason: the named reuse target cannot do the job, so §9 must cite the detector that already implements the rule (the census detector, with the reckon/interface_counts.py port as precedent) or drop the false reuse claim.
findings.text: §9 names clones.py's `functions_in` as the reader its write-then-replace inventory would extend, but `functions_in` parses the source and returns `_Function` token windows (reckon/clones.py:149-196), holding no AST node and no call, so it cannot detect the `os.replace`/`os.rename` or `.replace`/`.rename` call the rule turns on; the reading rule §9 describes already exists at docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233 `primitive_concepts`, which walks owned nodes and matches `os.replace`/`os.rename` and a one-arg `.replace`/`.rename` attribute

findings.reason: §9 should extend the owner's reader rather than fork a second walk over reckon/, which is precisely the reimplementation the plan exists to prevent.
findings.text: §9 stands up a new module walk plus definition reader inside a test, forking the walk already owned by `interface_counts.read_trees` (git ls-tree of every reckon/ module, parsed — reckon/interface_counts.py:326) and `interface_counts.definitions` (yields each definition's AST node, the exact input a call inspection needs — reckon/interface_counts.py:76), so the inventory's module set and parse drift from the counter that reads the same tree

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 hides temporary naming, the atomic rename, file fsync, mode and directory fsync behind one call, reckon/_store.py:419 `_write_through_sibling_temporary(path, render, *, fsync, mode, fsync_directory)`, and §9 collapses the remaining call sites onto it rather than adding wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 proposes a fresh AST walk over reckon/ plus its own definition reader in a new test while reckon/interface_counts.py:326 `read_trees` and :76 `definitions` already parse every module under reckon/ and yield its definition nodes.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 adds exactly one public definition and states the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted, §9 adds none and says so, and §7 adds none.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §9 cites reckon/clones.py:172 `functions_in` as the reader its AST inventory would extend, but that reader returns token windows and drops the AST, so it cannot see a call, and the exact call-detection rule §9 describes already exists at docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233 `primitive_concepts`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan promotes the existing owner primitive and deletes the private helpers; it introduces no layer over machinery without saying why that machinery cannot be extended.
